standard_prerequisites.name: Symmetric set with respect to a statistic
standard_prerequisites.statement: A is symmetric for D : A -> 2^{[N-1]} if the generating function sum over a in A of t^{D(a)} expands in standard Young tableaux with coefficients depending only on the shape.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis that produces equation (1) at source lines 620-623.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sparse statistic
standard_prerequisites.statement: D(a) is sparse if it contains no two consecutive integers.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used at source line 634 to rule out shapes with more than two parts.

standard_prerequisites.name: Superstandard tableau characterisations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The descent set of T_lambda determines the dominance order of the shape, and in the two-row case it determines the tableau and the shape uniquely.
standard_prerequisites.use: Lemma 1 at source lines 632-634 and Lemma 2 at source line 641 are the two inputs that turn the generating-function identity into the coefficient formula.

core_obligations: Apply the Schur-positivity criterion to A to obtain the expansion of the generating function over standard Young tableaux with Schur coefficients c_lambda, and reduce to showing c_lambda = |A(D = odds(k))| for lambda = (N-k,k) and c_lambda = 0 otherwise (source lines 620-624).
Assume A non-empty, pick a partition mu with c_mu different from 0 maximal in the conjugate order, and substitute J = Des(T_mu) into the refined identity for |A(D = J)| (source lines 626-632).

Use the first superstandard characterisation: any tableau with descent set Des(T_mu) is either T_mu itself or has a strictly larger conjugate shape, where c vanishes; hence |A(D = Des(T_mu))| = c_mu, which is non-zero (source lines 632-633).

Since the element realising Des(T_mu) has a sparse descent set while Des(T_mu) contains {1,2} whenever mu'_1 > 2, deduce mu'_1 <= 2 and therefore c_lambda = 0 for every partition with more than two parts (source lines 634-635).

Rewrite the identity with only two-row shapes and substitute J = Des(T_lambda) for lambda = (N-k,k), using the two-row characterisation to read off |A(D = odds(k))| = c_k, which is the stated expansion (source lines 636-641).

proof_roadmap.step: Criterion to generating-function expansion, reducing to the coefficients c_lambda.
Choose a maximal shape in conjugate order and substitute its descent set.
Extract c_mu and use sparsity to kill all shapes with more than two parts.
Restrict to two rows and identify the coefficients with the odd-set counts.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:if two rows and symmetric then schur positive` at source lines 612-618: if A is symmetric for a sparse statistic D then A is Schur-positive, with the explicit expansion Q_D(A) = sum over k of |A(D = odds(k))| s_{N-k,k}. The author's proof (source lines 619-642) is a multi-stage argument rather than a formal consequence of the criterion: it converts symmetry into the generating-function identity (lines 620-623), selects a Schur coefficient maximal in the conjugate order (line 626), evaluates the refined identity at the descent set of the corresponding superstandard tableau (lines 628-632) and uses the first superstandard characterisation to conclude that this coefficient is exactly |A(D = Des(T_mu))| and non-zero (lines 632-633). The key structural step is at lines 634-635, where sparsity of D(a) together with the appearance of {1,2} in Des(T_mu) forces the shape to have at most two parts and kills every other coefficient; only then does the two-row characterisation identify the remaining coefficients (line 641).
